messages:
erin: quick RFC follow-up: we need a defensible default for sampling quantization fallbacks across prod. aim: signal + safety with minimal perf impact.

mike: options: tagging-only (record signals), sync-high-prec for tiny pct, async-shadow copies, or hybrid. my leaning: tagging-only + tiny async shadow.

tara: ops constraints 1: no sync reroutes that touch user p95. shadows must be rate-limited per-region.

erin: propose defaults: tag_rate=1.0%, shadow_rate=0.03% globally. long-requests (>768 tokens) get tag_rate=3% and shadow_rate=0.1%. hysteresis: only enable per-tenant after 3 consecutive low-bit triggers.

leo: add trace labels: quant.sample=true, quant.shadow=true, quant.hysteresis_count=#. also include model_variant and tenant_id tags.

mike: telemetry: need quant.sample.count, quant.shadow.count, quant.quality.delta_p50, quant.quality.regression_rate, quant.shadow.token_overhead. slice by tenant and model.

erin: experiment plan: 2 weeks with defaults, compare to 1-week tagging-only baseline. threshold to consider rollback: regression_rate > 0.7% or p95 increase > 3ms attributable to sampling.

tara: infra: we'll cap concurrent shadows per-AZ and global token budget. i'll draft canary playbook and cost estimate.

leo: design question: shadows should use identical weights and seed for deterministic comparison. agree?
mike: yes, same weights to isolate quant effects.

erin: action items: mike add flags + trace labels, tara add infra caps + runbook, leo add telemetry dashboards/alerts. i'll update the RFC appendix with the chosen numbers.

infra-bot: deployment scheduled: quant-sampling-defaults v1 -> canary 2025-06-10 04:00 UTC.

erin: thanks, closing unless objections. :+1:
